abstract: Tumor evolution in lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD) drives drug resistance and disease progression, yet the cellular transitions underlying the malignant transformation of cells remain poorly understood. Comparing this progression of cancer cells across patients is challenging owing to substantial inter-patient cell heterogeneity. Here, based on single-nucleus RNA sequencing (snRNA-seq) data of 227 patients with LUAD including 422,727 tumor cells, we conducted a comprehensive investigation of tumor cell progression and developed Global Tumor Time (GTT), a continuous measure of tumor cell progression across patients. GTT provided a scalable and biologically meaningful metric of tumor progression that aligned with clinicopathological, transcriptomic and spatial characteristics of malignancy and demonstrated robust prognostic performance (C-index = 0.60), which was further validated in two external datasets comprising snRNA-seq (C-index = 0.66) and bulk RNA sequencing (C-index = 0.61). Using explainable AI to investigate the molecular correlates of GTT, we identified two distinct transcriptional programs associated with early and late progression states. These findings establish a scalable and interpretable framework for reconstructing malignant cell transformation across patients and allow for investigating the biology of tumor progression at single-cell resolution.
